chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

Isa ibn Ja'far ibn Isa asked Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him): About a woman who breastfed a boy for me, is it permissible for me to marry her husband's daughter? He said to me, 'How excellent is your question from here! It may be that people will say, 'His wife is forbidden to him because of the milk of this stallion.' This is the milk of the stallion, nothing else.' I said to him, 'Indeed, the girl is not the daughter of the woman who breastfed for me; she is the daughter of another.' He said, 'Even if there were ten scattered [women], nothing would be permissible for you from them, and they would be in the position of your daughters.'

key_terms.لَبَنُ الْفَحْلِ: Milk of the stallion (metaphor for the husband's milk connection via his wife)

ai.seo_question: Does the daughter of a woman who breastfed a man become his mahram through radāʿ?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the scope of *radāʿ* (milk kinship) by distinguishing between biological and non-biological daughters of the nursing woman. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the daughter of the husband, even if not biologically related to the nurse, is treated as a daughter for the purpose of marriage prohibition, illustrating the Shia juristic principle that milk kinship creates a permanent marital barrier akin to blood lineage.
